result.title: LATERAL ENTRY ADMISSION TO THE SECOND YEAR OF UG PROGRAMME (2026 -27)
result.summary: The partial document outlines the eligibility criteria and admission process for lateral entry into the second year of undergraduate (UG) programs for the academic year 2026-27. It specifies that candidates must have completed a diploma in a relevant discipline with a minimum duration of either three years after matriculation or two years after 10+2, with at least 60% marks (55% for SC/ST). Candidates must also possess good moral character and be Indian citizens. Admission is based on merit, prioritizing candidates with diplomas in relevant disciplines. If seats remain vacant, up to 10% of the sanctioned seats may be offered to candidates with diplomas in other disciplines. The document also lists various UG programs and their corresponding relevant diploma disciplines, such as Biomedical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Computer Engineering, and Electrical Engineering, among others.

nodes.title: ELIGIBILITY
nodes.summary: The partial document outlines the eligibility criteria and admission process for lateral entry into the second year of undergraduate engineering programs for the academic year 2026-27. It specifies that candidates must have completed a diploma in a relevant discipline with a minimum duration of two or three years, depending on their prior education, and must have secured at least 60% marks (55% for SC/ST candidates). The document emphasizes the importance of good moral character and Indian citizenship for eligibility. Admission is based on the merit of marks obtained in the diploma, with preference given to candidates from relevant disciplines. The document also lists the relevant diploma disciplines for various engineering programs, such as Biomedical, Chemical, Civil, Computer, Electrical, Electronics, Mechanical, Mechatronics, and Robotics & Artificial Intelligence. Additionally, it provides details on the number of seats available for each program, categorized by general, SC, ST, and PH categories, with a total of 324 seats available across all disciplines. Candidates can apply for multiple disciplines using a single application form with the required fee.

It covers various engineering disciplines available for lateral entry, including Electronics & Communication, Mechanical Engineering, and Robotics & Artificial Intelligence, among others. The document specifies the number of seats available for each discipline across different categories such as General, SC, ST, and PH, totaling 324 seats. It mentions a 1% seat reservation for children of institute employees and the possibility of filling vacant first-year seats through lateral entry. The tuition fee and application fee are stated, with the latter being Rs. 1500. The document also details scholarship opportunities for lateral entry students based on their diploma marks, offering different percentages of tuition fee waivers. Additionally, it mentions eligibility criteria for continued scholarships from the third year onwards, requiring a minimum CGPA and no backlogs. Merit-cum-means scholarships are also available for deserving students.

Additionally, students must maintain a minimum 8.50 CGPA and have no backlogs to continue receiving scholarships. Merit-cum-means scholarships are also available for deserving students. Further details can be found on the institute's admission website.

nodes.title: SCHOLARSHIP
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines the admission process and related details for lateral entry candidates at Thapar Institute of Engineering & Technology. Key points include:

1. **Reserved Seats**: 1% of seats are reserved for children of institute employees, with eligibility criteria specified.

2. **Vacant Seats**: Any vacant seats from the first year of the B.E./BTech 2025 batch will be filled by lateral entry candidates in the 2026-27 session.

3. **Fees**: Lateral entry candidates must pay the same tuition and other fees as those admitted in the 2026-27 session.

4. **Application Fee**: The application fee is Rs. 1500.

5. **Scholarships**: Merit scholarships are available for eligible lateral entry students based on diploma marks, with varying percentages of tuition fee waivers. Additionally, merit-cum-means scholarships are offered based on family income and academic performance.

6. **Admission Schedule**: Candidates can apply online, and the admission committee will handle document verification. Admission continues until seats are filled, with updates provided via the website and email.

7. **Important Notes**: 
   - Online application fee payment does not require sending a printout, but it must be presented at the interview.
   - If paid by DD, a printout must be sent with the DD.
   - Unfilled reserved category seats will be offered to general category candidates.
   - Candidates with pending backlogs are ineligible.
   - Tie-breaking criteria include age and marks in previous examinations.
   - Candidates appearing for their final qualifying exam can apply but must provide an undertaking during counselling.

2.6 ADMISSION SCHEDULE  
Candidates interested in taking admission in this programme can fill the application form 
available at https://admission.thapar.edu/ . Admission committee will contact the 
candidate for document verification. Admission will be offered to all the eligible 
candidates till the vacancy of seats exist. Candidates are advised to check the website 
and their registered email ID regularly for counselling schedule.  
 
2.7 IMPORTANT NOTE  
1 If Application Fee is paid Online : The candidates are not required to send the printout of 
application form but they must produce it at the time of interview .  
If Application Fee is paid through DD :  Please send one of the printouts by attaching DD 
of required amount as mentioned in filled online Application Form/Prospectus (in favour 
of Thapar Institute of Engineering & Technology and payable at Patiala) to “ In-charge 
Admission Cell’ Thapar Institute of Engineering & Technology, Patiala (Punjab) -147 004 . 
2 If any seat  in the reserve categories remained unfilled, such vacant seats shall be filled by 
General category candidates in the final round of counselling  on the basis of merit. In 
case a SC seat remains vacant, it will be first offered to ST candidate or a vice versa 
before converting into General Category.  
 
3 Candidates having any pending backlog in the qualifying degree ( diploma ) shall not be 
considered for admission.  
 
4 In case of a tie among candidates securing equal marks in the merit list, the same will be 
broken in accordance with the following criteria:  
a. Candidate senior in age shall rank higher in order of merit.   
 
b. In the case of a tie in percentage of marks in the qualifying examination also, a 
candidate securing higher percentage of marks in matriculation/secondary or 
equivalent examination shall rank higher in order of merit.   
 
5 Candidates appearing in the final exam of the qualifying degree are also eligible to 
apply. Such candidates have to furnish following undertaking at the time of counselling.

nodes.title: ADMISSION SCHEDULE
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines the criteria and process for awarding Merit-Cum-Means Scholarships for first-year and lateral entry students. Key points include the requirement for a gross family income of ≤ ₹10.00 lac and aggregate marks > 70% at the diploma level. Scholarships are awarded based on ascending order of income, with preference given to girl students from families with no male child in case of a tie. The scholarship committee consists of Deans and the Registrar. For subsequent years, criteria include a CGPA ≥ 7.50, adherence to income criteria, and no backlogs.

The document also details the admission schedule and process for a program at Thapar Institute of Engineering & Technology. Candidates can apply online, and admission is offered based on seat availability. Important notes include instructions for application fee payment, handling of unfilled reserved category seats, and criteria for breaking ties in merit. Candidates with pending backlogs are ineligible for admission, but those appearing for final exams can apply with an undertaking.

nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines the criteria and process for awarding Merit-Cum-Means Scholarships for first-year and lateral entry students. It specifies that the scholarship is based on a gross family income of ≤ ₹10.00 lac and requires aggregate marks of > 70% at the diploma level. Scholarships are awarded in ascending order of income, with preference given to girl students from families with no male child in case of a tie. The scholarship committee, consisting of Deans and the Registrar, finalizes the awards. For continuation from the second year onwards, students must maintain a CGPA of ≥ 7.50, meet the income criteria, and have no backlogs.

The document also details the admission schedule and process for a program, including the application procedure, document verification, and seat allocation based on merit. It highlights the importance of checking the website and email for updates. Important notes include instructions for application fee payment, handling of unfilled reserved category seats, and criteria for breaking ties in merit. Candidates with pending backlogs are ineligible for admission, but those appearing for their final exams can apply with an undertaking regarding their results.
